notes:
LENS C RETURNS ZERO FIELDS, AND THAT IS THE CORRECT ANSWER FOR THIS LENS ON THIS PAGE - it is a finding, not a gap. I started in tools-guides and exhausted it before opening admin-guides, as instructed. RESULT, MEASURED: the literal string 'Authorized Approval Limits' returns ZERO files in concur-invoice-professional-edition-tools-guides/ and exactly two in admin-guides (the two primaries). 'Approval Limit' returns exactly ONE tools-guides file (how-single-step-approval-workflow-works-40145f24.md) and it describes the WORKFLOWS sibling surface, not this window. Every one of the fourteen tools-guides files that mention User Administration defers to the external Shared: User Administration User Guide - I opened all fourteen and grepped each for 'user administration|approval limit|authorized approver|expense and invoice'; not one names a control in this window. So tools-guides carries this page's SCOPE and its downstream CONSUMPTION, and no field. Fields on this page are admin-guides-sourced and belong to the field-owning lens; emitting them here would risk a duplicate that bin/validate-graph.py cannot see.

WHAT I DID DELIVER: 21 dependencyCandidates and 5 contradictions, every quote grep -F verified at count >= 1 before writing (33 admin-guides anchors and 8 tools-guides anchors checked in two verification passes; no quote in this file was typed from memory, all were extracted from the files themselves).

DEPENDENCY FIELD NAMES ARE PREDICTIONS AND MUST BE RECONCILED AT MERGE. Because I emit no fields, the this-page endpoints of my dependencies use the names I expect the field-owning lens to emit: authorized_approval_limits_link, authorized_approval_limits_amount, authorized_approval_limits_currency, cost_object_approval_level, can_approve_exception, hierarchy_level_selector. If that lens names them differently the merge must re-point these edges rather than drop them. Workflows-side endpoints use the EXACT built names read out of output/kg-invoice-config.json: authorized_approver_feature_available_for_workflows, minimum_exception_level, maximum_exception_level, authorized_approver_approval_limit, authorized_approver_level. Three endpoints are deliberately unresolved forward references and should stay that way: cost_object_approver_feature (no built control activates it), user_record and invoice_approver_role and employee_import (external Shared guides absent from this corpus), non_po_workflow_options and invoice_approval_routing and single_step_approval_skip_rule and cost_object_approval_step and restrict_approvers_to_those_with_limit_authority (descriptive endpoints or already-built neighbours named for direction, not for re-homing).

uiVariant = undifferentiated, RE-MEASURED THIS RUN, NOT ASSUMED. Eight files corpus-wide carry new-experience / legacy / classic in their names; piping the two files that contain 'Authorized Approval Limits' through grep -ilE 'new experience|legacy|classic' returns ZERO. ONE HEDGE recorded and deliberately NOT acted on: tools-guides/how-single-step-approval-workflow-works-40145f24.md says the amounts are established using 'the Authorized Approvers link from workflows in the classic interface' (grep -F verified). That sentence describes the WORKFLOWS SIBLING surface reached under Administration > Invoice > Workflows, not this window, so it is NOT evidence of a variant here and I am not turning it into a fourth unearned 'both' claim. No field in this file carries uiVariant at all, since no field is emitted.

BOUNDARY VERDICT I TESTED AND ADOPTED, per control. The corpus states outright that three surfaces write one per-approver record ('Regardless of how the authorized approvers are entered into Invoice, they all appear in the Authorized Approver List.' - 86389a18, corroborated by 8b3be88b, 82481079, 3966259c, 8b3c119a and 8b3c5273: six attestations). So the surfaces are distinct UI presentations of one underlying record, and this window's controls are real fields - but the AMOUNT here must never be labelled 'Approval Limit'. This window presents an unnamed Approval Limit AREA holding a currency selector and an Amount field; branch A presents two further, differently-named controls (Manager Approval Limit, Approval Limit Currency list); only Workflows has a control literally named 'Approval Limit'. A fifth 'Approval Limit' is the exact duplicate this run exists to avoid. CONFIRMED NEGATIVE, and I agree with it: there is NO Approver control on this page. On Workflows you select an approver because you are creating a list row via New; here the approver is the record context you arrived with. Neither primary names an Approver control anywhere in its full description of the window. Do not emit a twin of field.workflows.authorized-approver-list-approver.

WHAT THE DOCUMENTATION DOES NOT DETERMINE, stated plainly rather than papered over: (1) whether the Level control genuinely exists in this window - two files disagree flatly and I recorded both; (2) whether clearing the currency is part of the unlimited recipe on this surface; (3) whether the two branch renderings are one page or two - I agree with the one-page reading on the strength of the single step-4 row in 8a960238 marked X under BOTH deployment columns ('Assign the proper rights to users using one or more of these:'), but no corpus topic names a second page, so this is a judgement, not a documented fact; (4) whether this window has a Save button - only branch A documents 'clicks Save', and the window itself never does; (5) the valid currency values - NO enumerated currency list exists anywhere in this corpus, only the constraint that the code is 3 characters and must be a valid system reimbursement currency, so validValues for any currency control must remain [] and no valueSetCandidate could honestly be built. That is why valueSetCandidates and compressedRanges are both empty here: nothing in the corpus is enumerated or compressed for this page.

SCOPE, NOT NEGOTIABLE AND STATED POSITIVELY: this is Invoice configuration reached through the Company admin menu. It is the first page in this graph not reached under Administration > Invoice, which matters enormously to a driver, but menu location is a navigation fact and says nothing about which product a control configures. Nothing in this file says or implies otherwise.

THREE BUILT NODES CARRY STALE PROSE THAT THIS RUN REVERSES and the merge must repair, not leave standing: dep.gworkflows.060 (its condition asserts this window 'is not a page to build' and points at an unresolved forward reference this run resolves), vset.gworkflows.unnamed.two-further-named-feature-hierarchies-attested-in-the-corpus, and vset.gworkflows.unnamed.the-four-configuration-steps-for-authorized-approvers-and-wh. None of the three mines a field from fcfd570c or 8a960238, so nothing is being re-homed - only the reversed scope language needs fixing.
